Decisions - human verdicts (read, never invented)

What the verdict words mean - the full outcome set

Stage and milestone outcomes come from the outcome matrix (BUILD-PLAYBOOK §4.4): every retrospective ends in exactly one of the four outcomes below. This ledger also records the additional verdict vocabularies listed after them.

  • Sound - every hard gate and every soft gate passed - the stage proceeds as-is.
  • Sound but rough - hard gates passed, one or two soft gates failed - playbook/templates get revised first, then the work proceeds.
  • Friction-heavy - hard gates passed but three or more soft gates failed - stop and iterate on the process before the next stage.
  • Not ready - a hard gate failed - diagnose and fix before proceeding; the stage does not close.
  • score 5 - a pre-cutover user stamp: the owner's 1–5 stage score, recorded verbatim (the numeric stamps predate the pass/fail stamp cutover and are grandfathered, never rewritten).
  • score 4 - a pre-cutover user stamp: the owner's 1–5 stage score, recorded verbatim (the numeric stamps predate the pass/fail stamp cutover and are grandfathered, never rewritten).
  • pass - the owner's user-friction stamp at stage close, recorded verbatim.
  • fail - the owner's user-friction stamp at stage close, recorded verbatim.
  • UNKNOWN - the source document carries no structured verdict line; the row below quotes what was read there, and no verdict is inferred from it.

THE LEDGER NAMED TWO READERS; THE LIVE SWEEP FOUND FOUR — TD-068's Affected line names the SessionStart + mode-check readers, but the pretooluse red-gate (readMode) and receipts-lifecycle (resolveRole) carried the same fallback, and removing only the two named would have left the red-gate and the receipts ledger honoring a marker the session layer ignores, which is strictly worse than the open window because the layers would then disagree. MEASURED on the pre-implementation tree with .claude/active-mode=verifier planted and NO .claude/role: SessionStart stamped role=verifier; mode-check passed a verifier prompt and blocked a work prompt; receipts-lifecycle emitted role:"verifier" into the ledger; and — the one with teeth — THE RED-GATE ALLOWED AN IMPLEMENTATION EDIT DURING AN OPEN, UN-APPROVED STAGE (exit 0), i.e. a retired marker could DISENGAGE PROC-001. All four now read role-absent → the `work` default. STATED, NOT BLURRED: this is a CONTRACT CHANGE, not a defect fix — nothing is destroyed, a retired file is simply no longer consulted, and TD-068 itself named re-bootstrapping or re-running set-mode.cjs as the migration the window existed to buy time for. THE CARVE-OUT RULING IS STRICT AND OWNER-RATIFIED: ROLE_ALIAS_MARKER is deleted from both validator twins with NO replacement carve-out, so role_terms now has ZERO exemptions — the end-state its own header comment always described — which forces the persistence note to record the close WITHOUT naming the retired file; the filename survives only in the historical records (docs/tech-debt.md, CHANGELOG.md), which the class does not scan, and F-p8a asserts that the very sentence M20.B carved out is now NAMED as drift. THE M28.C ALLOWLIST EXPIRY FIRED FOR THE FIRST TIME: item 6 emptied both TD-068 sites, making both dated PHANTOM-guarded entries phantoms, and they were deleted in the same pass — C-p6b now POSITIVELY REJECTS a surviving TD-068 entry rather than merely omitting it from its expectation, and its staleness bound advanced M28.C → M28.F so any entry dated to a stage that has already run is overdue by definition. DELIBERATELY KEPT, each pinned so a later stage cannot quietly tidy it away: both .gitignore entries for the retired name (nothing writes it, but a pre-M28 project can still have one on disk and it must stay uncommittable — F-p14) and the `> .claude/active-mode` raw-redirect ban (the truncate-write hazard is name-agnostic; a stale tutorial can still teach it). RED-first: 31 pins in ONE addressable section (SECTION_META id `alias-window`, the M28.B extension protocol — data plus one audit run), 19 RED before implementation, 12 controls/teeth green-by-design and each labelled as such in source including F-p12b, which is green on BOTH sides and says so rather than being counted as a win; two further pins RED in older sections (the writer header; the assembled-payload wording lock). Mutations: restore the fallback in ONE reader → F-p1 REDs ALONE among the four behavior pins (per-reader teeth); restore the second marker write → F-p5b REDs ALONE. RETIREMENT MAPPING, not a bare count: ELEVEN pins asserted the window — 7 RETIRED (their property ceased to exist with the window, each with its inverse named), 2 re-pointed whose surviving half already held (green-before, and a re-point that keeps only the true half CANNOT be RED-before), and 2 re-pointed RED-before (the set-mode header and [M25.F · alias-window-wording], both of which required a FUTURE retirement boundary that has now arrived) — 7+2+2=11, one retired check per retired pin. The count is eleven and not ten because the carve-out was asserted TWICE, in two sections ([M20.A · role] and [M20.B·naming-lock teeth], defence in depth); an earlier draft of the mapping listed only the second, and the label diff caught the omission by disagreeing with it (7 removals against 6 tabled retirements) — which is the argument for deriving the mapping from the diff rather than from memory. Assurance

In plain terms: a record here is one entry the collectors derived from the project's committed history - its retrospectives, Verifier findings files, CHANGELOG lines, the tech-debt and release-state ledgers, and git itself. Each of the 1566 collected records was checked against the receipt schema (software-build-assurance-kit/build-receipt/v1); all 1566 parse as valid statements. What that check proved: every claim on this page traces to a schema-valid record - none was dropped, none was rewritten.

  • 1566 records → 1566 valid software-build-assurance-kit/build-receipt/v1 statements
  • unclassified records: 1179 - these matched no known event class, so they are counted and shown as unknown, never forced into a bin. That is the kit's unknowns-shown-as-unknown rule working as designed, not confusion: a class is assigned only when a record's own bytes match a defined pattern.
What does unclassified mean here?

What a record is, versus a classified event: the collectors read the committed history - retrospectives, Verifier findings files, CHANGELOG lines, the tech-debt and release-state ledgers, and git itself - and pull out entries. The report knows how to summarize 8 specific record types from that history: stage-rework, control, verifier-finding, commit, milestone, milestone-complete, release-transition, tech-debt. Each classified entry lands in one of the four lists above (BAU, worked, broke, shipped).

What the 1179 unclassified are: real entries from that same history that match none of those types - history contains more kinds of lines than the report classifies. By the classifier's own rules this includes every tech-debt entry (deferred backlog, never forced into a bin), any commit that is not a stage-shaped commit, and any rework row whose budget was never declared. This frozen snapshot stores the count, not the entries or a per-kind breakdown, so the composition cannot be shown here - stated rather than invented. The capture gap is recorded on the kit's tech-debt ledger; a model that carries the breakdown renders it in place of this sentence.

What it means for the numbers: every classified-record summary on this page counts only classified entries; the unclassified are counted and disclosed so the totals stay honest - nothing was silently dropped, and nothing unknown was dressed up as known. The arithmetic is on the page: 1566 records = 387 classified + 1179 unclassified.

Why that is a feature: the alternative is a report that either hides what it did not understand or mislabels it - this one shows its remainder.

Limitations - what this report does NOT claim

  • deferred backlog item — a limitations-section input, not a build outcome; derived from committed history; no lifecycle events for this range, so role/turn durations are unknown (pre-instrumentation), never zeroed
  • derived completion — requires BOTH the closeout commit and the release-state row; derived from committed history; no lifecycle events for this range, so role/turn durations are unknown (pre-instrumentation), never zeroed
  • hash/subject/date only; author identity omitted (J4 — pending the render-stage sanitizer); derived from committed history; no lifecycle events for this range, so role/turn durations are unknown (pre-instrumentation), never zeroed
  • rework/budget read from the retro PROSE (fallback; not the fenced block); derived from committed history; no lifecycle events for this range, so role/turn durations are unknown (pre-instrumentation), never zeroed
  • rework/budget read from the retro fenced block; derived from committed history; no lifecycle events for this range, so role/turn durations are unknown (pre-instrumentation), never zeroed
  • severity read from the finding heading marker; fixed only from a structured status: or fix: line, rendered as written; derived from committed history; no lifecycle events for this range, so role/turn durations are unknown (pre-instrumentation), never zeroed
  • transition parsed from the release-state ledger; derived from committed history; no lifecycle events for this range, so role/turn durations are unknown (pre-instrumentation), never zeroed
  • verdict read only from a structured verdict: line in the closed vocabulary; FNR read from the CHANGELOG text, not recomputed; derived from committed history; no lifecycle events for this range, so role/turn durations are unknown (pre-instrumentation), never zeroed
